title: Transport a linearity criterion across a ring-sheaf isomorphism
statement: Let $U,V$ be schemes and $f:U\to V$ a morphism on their small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $R_V,R_U$ be commutative ring sheaves, $L_r$ a left adjoint to the ring direct image with adjunction $a_r$, $c:L_r(R_V)\cong R_U$, and $\gamma:R_V\to f_*R_U$ the adjunct of $c$. Write $F_V,F_0,F_U$ for forgetting modules over $R_V,L_r(R_V),R_U$ to abelian sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $a:L_a\dashv R_a$ for the etale abelian adjunction. Suppose $L_0:\operatorname{Mod}(R_V)\to\operatorname{Mod}(L_r(R_V))$ and $e_0:L_0F_0\cong F_VL_a$ are given. Assume that for every $G,F$ and abelian map $\alpha:L_aF_VG\to F_0F$, a linear lift $h:L_0G\to F$ with $F_0h=e_0(G)\alpha$ exists iff the abelian adjunct of $\alpha$ lifts to an $R_V$-linear map $G\to R_0F$, where $R_0$ is direct image along $a_r$'s ring unit [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Then there exist $L_M:\operatorname{Mod}(R_V)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_U)$, $e:L_MF_U\cong F_VL_a$, $t:L_M\operatorname{res}_c\cong L_0$, and $a_M:L_M\dashv f_{*,\gamma}$. For every $G$, $F_0(t_G)e_{0,G}=e_G$. For every linear $h:L_MG\to F$, $F_V(a_M(h))=a(e_G^{-1}F_Uh)$.

proof.text: Construct LM as L0 followed by restriction along c.inv. Restriction along c.hom and c.inv are inverse functors up to natural identity-on-section comparisons: their composite scalar actions agree with the original action by the inverse-ring identities. They induce t and e.

Apply the assumed linearity criterion to the same underlying map with the target restricted along c.hom. The adjunct identity gives gamma = ar.unit.app RV followed by direct image of c.hom. Thus restricting direct image along the ring unit is direct image along gamma. Linear maps and their underlying hom equivalence agree under these identifications.

The faithful forgetful functors make the linear lifts unique. Restrict the abelian hom equivalence to the two sets of linear maps. Its naturality gives am; its formula is the required hom comparison. The identity-on-sections comparison gives the equation relating t, e0, and e.
